tool_args.old_string:
\paragraph{Measurement error in causal inference.}
Foundations appear in \citet{carroll2006, gustafson2004, buonaccorsi2010, bound2001measurement}, with DAG-based formalization by \citet{hernan_cole2009} and \citet{kuroki_pearl2014}. For binary variables, non-differential misclassification biases toward the null~\cite{bross1954misclassification, brenner1993, ogburn_vanderweele2012}, but this fails for polytomous exposures~\cite{dosemeci1990, jurek2005, veirod_laake2001}. Extensions address differential measurement error~\cite{edwards_lessler_naimi2021, imai_yamamoto2010}, endogenous misreporting~\cite{nguimkeu_denteh_tchernis2019}, mismeasured covariates under IPW~\cite{shu_yi2019a, shu_yi2019b}, mediation with mismeasured mediators~\cite{valeri_vanderweele2013}, nonclassical error~\cite{schennach2020mismeasured}, and multiply robust estimation~\cite{wei2025multiply}. All analyze a single DAG topology; ours characterizes how the same confusion matrix produces qualitatively different bias across seven topologies.
tool_args.new_string:
\paragraph{Measurement error in causal inference.}
Foundations appear in \citet{carroll2006, gustafson2004, buonaccorsi2010, bound2001measurement}, with DAG-based formalization by \citet{hernan_cole2009} and \citet{kuroki_pearl2014}. For binary variables, non-differential misclassification biases toward the null~\cite{bross1954misclassification, brenner1993, ogburn_vanderweele2012}, but this fails for polytomous exposures~\cite{dosemeci1990, jurek2005, veirod_laake2001}. Extensions address differential error~\cite{edwards_lessler_naimi2021, imai_yamamoto2010}, mismeasured covariates~\cite{shu_yi2019a, shu_yi2019b}, mediation~\cite{valeri_vanderweele2013}, and nonclassical error~\cite{schennach2020mismeasured, nguimkeu_denteh_tchernis2019, wei2025multiply}. All analyze a single DAG; ours characterizes how the same confusion matrix produces qualitatively different bias across seven topologies.

tool_args.old_string:
\paragraph{Text classifiers and LLM annotation.}
\citet{grimmer2022} and \citet{feder_etal2022} provide foundations for text-as-data and causal inference in NLP. \citet{wood_doughty2018} first applied DAG reasoning to classifier error; \citet{teblunthuis2024} gave the most complete binary treatment ($K{=}2$, four DAGs); \citet{lee_wood_doughty2024} extended to categorical LLM classifiers but covered only confounding. On annotation quality, \citet{gilardi2023chatgpt} and \citet{ziems2024can} document rapid LLM annotator adoption (surveyed by \citealt{tan2024llm}), \citet{baumann2025} found 31\% incorrect conclusions, and \citet{kim_garg2025} showed 60\% error correlation across models~\cite{pangakis_wolken_fasching2023, cheng_mayya_sedoc2024, variance_aware_llm2026, hidden_measurement_error2026}. \citet{audinet2025} benchmark debiasing; \citet{keith_jensen_oconnor2020} survey the landscape. These works either restrict to binary labels, cover a single topology, or diagnose quality without connecting it to causal validity.
tool_args.new_string:
\paragraph{Text classifiers and LLM annotation.}
\citet{grimmer2022} and \citet{feder_etal2022} provide foundations for text-as-data causal inference. \citet{wood_doughty2018} first applied DAG reasoning to classifier error; \citet{teblunthuis2024} gave the most complete binary treatment ($K{=}2$, four DAGs); \citet{lee_wood_doughty2024} extended to categorical LLM classifiers but covered only confounding. On annotation quality, \citet{gilardi2023chatgpt} and \citet{ziems2024can} document rapid LLM adoption~\cite{tan2024llm}, \citet{baumann2025} found 31\% incorrect conclusions, and \citet{kim_garg2025} showed 60\% error correlation~\cite{pangakis_wolken_fasching2023, cheng_mayya_sedoc2024, audinet2025, keith_jensen_oconnor2020, variance_aware_llm2026, hidden_measurement_error2026}. tool_args.old_string:
\paragraph{Sensitivity analysis and correction methods.}
Our ASV framework draws on sensitivity analysis without assumptions~\cite{ding_vanderweele2016}, E-values~\cite{vanderweele_ding2017, mathur2018}, robustness values~\cite{cinelli2020making}, and mediation sensitivity~\cite{imai_keele_yamamoto2010, pryzant_etal2021}, but parametrizes annotation error severity rather than omitted variable strength. \citet{lash2009} and \citet{blackwell_honaker_king2017} provide complementary frameworks; \citet{mahajan2006} and \citet{hu2008} establish identification and estimation under misclassified regressors, including nonlinear models with instrumental variables. For correction, PPI++~\cite{angelopoulos2023} and DSL~\cite{egami_hinck_stewart_wei2023} are topology-agnostic, with extensions by \citet{zrnic_candes2024, demirel2024prediction, cadei2025, gligoric2025}. We show this agnosticism is costly: correction effectiveness is itself topology-dependent, with matrix-based methods provably ineffective under linear FWL decomposition for four topologies.
tool_args.new_string:
\paragraph{Sensitivity analysis and correction methods.}
Our ASV framework draws on E-values~\cite{vanderweele_ding2017, mathur2018}, robustness values~\cite{cinelli2020making}, and mediation sensitivity~\cite{imai_keele_yamamoto2010, ding_vanderweele2016, pryzant_etal2021}, but parametrizes annotation error severity rather than omitted variable strength. \citet{lash2009}, \citet{blackwell_honaker_king2017}, \citet{mahajan2006}, and \citet{hu2008} provide complementary frameworks for misclassified regressors. For correction, PPI++~\cite{angelopoulos2023} and DSL~\cite{egami_hinck_stewart_wei2023} are topology-agnostic~\cite{zrnic_candes2024, demirel2024prediction, cadei2025, gligoric2025}. We show this agnosticism is costly: correction effectiveness is topology-dependent, with matrix-based methods provably ineffective under FWL decomposition for four topologies.

tool_args.old_string:
\paragraph{Notation conventions.}
Our analysis characterizes probability limits (plim, $N \to \infty$) rather than finite-sample variance. The FWL theorem~\cite{frisch1933partial} guarantees that each regression coefficient equals the coefficient from a simple regression after residualizing all other variables---this is why matrix-based corrections fail for covariate topologies (Section~\ref{sec:correction}). Table~\ref{tab:notation} (Appendix~\ref{app:notation_table}) collects all notation.
tool_args.new_string:
\paragraph{Notation conventions.}
Our analysis characterizes probability limits ($N \to \infty$) under the FWL theorem~\cite{frisch1933partial}, which explains why matrix-based corrections fail for covariate topologies (Section~\ref{sec:correction}). Notation is collected in Table~\ref{tab:notation} (Appendix~\ref{app:notation_table}).

tool_args.old_string: In batch annotation pipelines, the LLM processes each text independently without access to $Y$, making non-differentiality an architectural invariant~\cite{ziems2024can}; Y-stratified permutation tests confirm this (1/12 rejection at $\alpha{=}0.05$; Appendix~\ref{sec:y_stratified_test}). Non-differentiality holds architecturally when $Y$ is external to the annotated text (e.g., health outcomes, voting behavior), since the LLM cannot condition on unobserved $Y$; it may be violated when $Y$ correlates with text content (e.g., topic), in which case the Y-stratified test (Appendix~\ref{sec:y_stratified_test}) provides empirical verification. Under stress testing, sign reversal occurs in 14/16 $K{\geq}3$ exposure configurations at $\varepsilon{=}0.01$ structured departure, with sign-flip rate increasing from 2.0\% to 9.67\% at $\varepsilon{=}0.20$ (Appendix~\ref{sec:nondiff_stress}); formal degradation guarantees under differential misclassification remain an open problem.

正文共 ~17 处解释性 em-dash (`---`)，是最显著的 AI 写作痕迹。**全部替换为逗号、分号、括号或拆句。** 具体位置：

**注意**：Frisch--Waugh--Lovell、Cauchy--Schwarz 等专有名词的 en-dash (`--`) 是正确用法，不要改。只改解释性的 em-dash (`---`)。
